user_text: Thoracic surgery teams need a dual-lumen chest drainage catheter that keeps two independent lumens patent while passing through a 9-millimeter intercostal space: the current 4.0-millimeter-outer catheter kinks when the lumens exceed 60 percent of the wall area, and suction collapses the septum at 25 kilopascals. Design a circular dual-lumen catheter with an outer diameter between 6 and 8 millimeters, two equal circular lumens of 2.2 to 2.8 millimeters each, a septum thickness between 0.6 and 1.2 millimeters, and a working length of 300 to 500 millimeters, that resists kinking under a 15-millimeter bend radius and withstands 40 kilopascals of suction without septum collapse.
